selected.description: Type spelling changed between ABI-identical types: SplitNodeDescriptor double -> feature_t (same size, alignment and register class; a source-level change only)
selected.impact: A parameter, return, field or variable was retyped between two types the compiler passes, stores and returns identically (same size, alignment and register class: long -> long long on LP64, char -> signed char, an enum -> its unsigned underlying integer, __int128 -> unsigned __int128, a float vector -> a double of the same size). The compiled ABI is unchanged, so an existing binary keeps working. The declared type is different, though: a source that overloads on it, a template instantiated over it, or a function pointer of the old type can see the difference, so the change is recorded as a source-level risk.
